content: Luxury developer marketing sites (2026) cluster around four buyer-journey layers: master plan (orient) -> building/tower explorer (choose) -> floor plan (compare) -> unit detail (decide). Interactive 3D/360 is now table stakes for premium launches: unit-specific pages with specs and floor plans, 360 photo/video scenes, per-unit shareable URLs, POI hotspots, and lead capture embedded inside the tour rather than only at page end. Vendors (UnitFinder/Plyo, RegalScene, RFX Plus, Render Vision, Matterport) sell 'interactive building explorer' where units are clickable hotspots on exterior renders, colour-coded by availability, deep-zoom to a floor/unit, with enquire-in-context. Trends to treat cautiously: brochure-on-demand PDF generation, sun-path simulation, 3D availability colouring on the public site, and 'measure inside the tour' features - all add asset/ops cost and can conflict with a no-public-pricing policy. Live guided remote tours exist but imply staffing.
